newsitem.title: USA: Amoco renews call for quick Baltic resolution.
newsitem.headline: Amoco renews call for quick Baltic resolution.

text.p: Amoco Corp on Wednesday renewed its request that Lithuania and Latvia speedily resolve their border dispute in the Baltic Sea so exploration of a promising oil prospect can continue.

A Latvian Radio report Wednesday claimed Amoco, at a meeting in Washington with Vytautas Landsbergis, the speaker of the Lithuanian parliament and a former president of the country, had threatened to abandon the project if Lithuania's demarcation dispute with Latvia wasn't resolved soon.
However, an Amoco spokesman said the company's representative merely reiterated to Landsbergis that progress on the project hinges on a resolution of the dispute.

"We haven't issued any warnings, we made no threats. At his request, we met with (Landsbergis) on Monday of this week at the Lithuanian embassy in Washington...(and) we reiterated that the project can't go forward until the issue is resolved," said Jim Spangler, a spokesman for Amoco.

The project is a 50/50 joint venture between Amoco and OPAB, a unit of Swedish oil group Svenska Petroleum. The exploration prospect lies half in Swedish waters and half in waters disputed by the two former Soviet republics, in about 120 meters depth.
The agreement requires a three-year commitment to assess the area, including at least one exploration well drilled within that period.
Amoco has purchased seismic data on the area and said it is a "very interesting" prospect, but also noted that it doesn't fall within its six "strategic growth areas."

The Lithuanian government has linked discussion of exploration of the prospect to other talks for some form of joint venture involving its 240,000 barrels per day Mazeikia refinery, as well as other downstream interests, oil industry sources said.
